question: Two non-exempt employees under the ordinary provincial overtime rules each work six seven-hour days in one workweek, with no special averaging or overtime agreement. One works in Alberta and the other in Manitoba. How many overtime hours arise from this schedule in each province?

The Alberta Labour Code provides that an employee is entitled to overtime pay for any work performed in excess of eight hours in a day or 40 hours in a week. The Code also provides that an employee is entitled to overtime pay for any work performed on a day of rest. In this case, the employee worked six seven-hour days in one workweek, for a total of 42 hours. This is two hours in excess of the 40-hour weekly maximum, and therefore the employee is entitled to two hours of overtime pay. 2. Manitoba

The Manitoba Labour Standards Act provides that an employee is entitled to overtime pay for any work performed in excess of eight hours in a day or 40 hours in a week. This is two hours in excess of the 40-hour weekly maximum, and therefore the employee is entitled to two hours of overtime pay. 3. Comparison

In both Alberta and Manitoba, the employee is entitled to two hours of overtime pay for working six seven-hour days in one workweek. This is because the employee worked two hours in excess of the 40-hour weekly maximum in each province.
